name: limit_edge_that_does_not_exist
why: THE TWIN OF `drawing_dimensions_itself` (entry F5): a refusal is never alone. A proof that verifies only the refusal does not tell «the check works» from «the operation refuses everything» — and here the green twin really exists, which `model_dimensions` lacks and which prevented writing its case on the refusal.
_what_changes_compared_to_the_twin: One argument: `edges`. The twin does not say it and dimensions the first four; this one asks for edge **999**, which is not there. Same operation, same drawing, same part.
defect_caught: An operation that, asked for an edge that does not exist, dimensions **another one** and answers «done». The drawing would come out dimensioned, with the dimension attached to the wrong thing, and nobody would say anything. The refusal must say **how many edges the view has**, because it is the information needed to ask for the right one: *a refusal that does not say the alternative leaves the reader to guess exactly what the operation has stopped guessing.*

a view attaches to the path of the part
